title: How to Apply for an NBI Clearance in the Philippines
description: Secure your official background clearance for employment and travel requirements.

requirements.title: Two (2) Valid IDs
requirements.description: Government-issued IDs with photo and signature.

requirements.title: Online Appointment Receipt
requirements.description: Printed or digital copy of your NBI appointment.

requirements.title: Active Email Address
requirements.description: For receiving updates and your e-clearance.

requirements.title: Personal Information
requirements.description: Complete details (name, birth date, address, etc.)

checklist.title: Register Online Account
checklist.description: Create an account and complete the online application form.

checklist.title: Pay Application Fee
checklist.description: Pay the corresponding fee at any Bayad Center or online.

checklist.title: Visit NBI Branch
checklist.description: Go to your chosen NBI branch on your appointment date.

checklist.title: Biometrics & Photo
checklist.description: Provide your biometrics and have your photo taken.

blocks.content: An **NBI Clearance** is an official document issued by the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) in the Philippines. It is a mandatory requirement for most legal, employment, and travel-related transactions in the country.
It serves as proof that an individual does not have a criminal record, pending criminal case, or derogatory record based on the NBI's centralized national database.

The clearance is commonly required for:
*   **Employment:** Local and overseas job applications.
*   **Travel:** Passport and Visa processing.
*   **Professionalism:** Government transactions & Professional Licenses (PRC).
*   **Legal:** Business requirements & court-related documentation.
*   **Education:** School enrollment and scholarship applications.
The NBI Clearance is one of the most widely accepted and trusted government-issued clearance documents in the Philippines.
**Pro Tip:** Fresh graduates can get this for FREE under the First-Time Jobseekers Act. Bring your Barangay Certificate of First-Time Jobseeker.

You may need an NBI Clearance if you are:
- Applying for a new job or a promotion.
- Working abroad or processing immigration papers.
- Applying for a Philippine passport or a foreign visa.
- Processing professional licenses with the PRC.
- Starting a business or applying for local permits.
- Completing legal or court-related requirements.
**Note:** First-time applicants are required to register online before visiting an NBI branch for biometrics capture.

content.title: Benefits of Having an NBI Clearance

blocks.title: Employment Requirement
blocks.content: Most employers in the Philippines require a valid NBI Clearance before hiring to ensure the integrity of their workforce.

blocks.title: Proof of Good Standing
blocks.content: The clearance helps verify that you have no criminal records or pending cases nationwide, which is essential for many civil transactions.

blocks.title: Travel and Visa Applications
blocks.content: Embassies and overseas employers request an NBI Clearance as part of their standard background verification for applicants.

blocks.title: Online Registration (Portal)
blocks.content: The standard method for all applicants to schedule appointments and pay fees is via the official portal.

blocks.title: NBI Clearance Mobile App
blocks.content: You can now apply and pay directly through the official NBI Clearance mobile app, which is often faster for renewals.

blocks.title: NBI Clearance "Quick Renewal"
blocks.content: For those whose clearance expired between 2014 and the present, you can use the "Quick Renewal" service for home delivery without visiting a branch, provided no changes are needed to your personal data.

blocks.title: Create an Online Account
blocks.content: Register through the official NBI portal. Provide an active email address as you will receive your **Reference Number** and notifications there.

blocks.title: Fill Out the Application Form
blocks.content: Complete your personal information carefully. Ensure that your name, civil status, and birth details match your valid IDs and PSA records exactly.

blocks.title: Select Your Appointment Schedule
blocks.content: Choose your preferred NBI branch and a time slot.
Some popular branches (like NBI Main or mall-based satellite offices) fill up weeks in advance.

blocks.title: Pay the NBI Clearance Fee
blocks.content: After scheduling, pay via GCash, Maya, or other payment centers. **Save the Reference Number**—you cannot proceed at the branch without it.

blocks.title: Visit the NBI Branch
blocks.content: Arrive at your selected branch on your appointment date. Bring your valid IDs and the Reference Number.

blocks.title: Biometrics and Image Capture
blocks.content: Undergo fingerprint scanning and photo capture. If you have a "Hit," you will be asked to return after a few days.

blocks.title: Claim Your Clearance
blocks.content: If you have "No Hit," your clearance is usually released within minutes. If you have a "Hit," wait for the advised release date (usually 10 working days).

For the most accurate and up-to-date information, please visit:
- [Official NBI Clearance Portal](https://clearance.nbi.gov.ph)
- [National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Official Website](https://www.nbi.gov.ph)

items: **"With Hit" Status:** This means your name matches a person with a criminal record in the NBI database. It requires manual verification by an NBI agent, which typically takes 8–10 working days.
**Reference Number Not Received:** Check your spam folder or log in to the portal to view your transaction history.
**Apply for Renewal via App:** If you've had a clearance before, using the official app is much faster.
**Avoid Peak Days:** Mondays and Fridays are typically the busiest days. Mid-week appointments are usually smoother.
**Use the First-Time Jobseeker Act:** If you're a fresh graduate, get the certificate from your Barangay first. Presenting this at the NBI branch will waive the ₱130 fee under **RA 11261**.

blocks.content: **Note:** A 'HIT' is common and usually just means a manual name check. Don't panic; it just adds about 8-10 working days to your release.

blocks.title: What does "With Hit" mean?
blocks.content: A "hit" simply means your name (or a very similar one) exists in the NBI's database of people with criminal records. It does **not** necessarily mean you have a record; it just requires NBI to verify you aren't the person in question.

blocks.title: How long is the NBI Clearance valid?
blocks.content: The NBI Clearance is valid for **one (1) year** from the date of issuance.
